event: Elsie wakes in the attic room to bread-smell and lake mist on the round window.
She greets her four potted plants by name, then washes at the cold basin.
She laces her novice's cream halter, hands unsteady, and clips the flower above one ear.

changes.note: Elsie laces the novice's outfit on: worn at the body
Flower clip put on above one ear

event: She seals the week's letter, counts her coins, and packs the satchel: salve, bandages.

changes.note: Elsie counts her coins: her purse is shown

event: Elsie eats a warm roll at the bakery, and the baker waves her out.
She posts the letter at the corner shop; two women go by arm in arm.
The Hall of Naming stands white above the lake, its glass dome full of morning.
The girl ahead asks if she is nervous; Elsie says yes, and warms her cold hands.
Inside, a priestess calls the names; the first girl's window opens above her.
Elsie hopes for simples; then her turn comes, and she steps into the circle.
It reads: Enthraller.

changes.note: Class: Enthraller; the Naming window names it

event: She reads it twice; the silence spreads outward and nobody in the hall moves.
A woman in the gallery takes her child and leaves; the priestess calls no next name.
Elsie says, Oh! that sounds like a lot of responsibility, and steps down.
The hall does not clap; outside, the others from the line look at her and away.
She walks down from the hall alone, and the city is warm and ordinary around her.
The guild hall is timber and noise, its green copper roof across Brightwater Square.
In the registration line, the clerk takes her name and asks her class.
She says Enthraller; the clerk's pen stops, and he goes up the stairs.
The guildmaster comes down, grey and sword-calloused, and takes Elsie up.
She reads the Strings Accord: every skill reported, none on anyone unwilling.
Told the watching is so nothing goes wrong, Elsie says she is glad of it.
She counts the fee onto the desk; the clerk stamps a copper tag with an F.

changes.note: Rank: F; the clerk stamps her copper tag
Guild registration fee, two lanterns: 134 -> 114 pips
Guild registration fee, two lanterns: purse 114 pips

event: The guildmaster opens the charcoal door: a young woman stands with a black ledger.
Warden Corisande Vane, called Cora, will go with her and write down every skill.
Cora will report each to the guildmaster; Elsie thanks her for coming.
Cora does not answer; Elsie asks what she likes in her tea.
Cora says: black and strong, one sugar; Elsie says she will remember it.
Back in the hall, Elsie reads the F-rank notices, then finds the party board.
Parties look each other over and nobody looks at her; the slates she asks are full.
The fourth slate is turned to the wall; the cast-offs' slates stand at the corner.
A woman with a great axe strapped across her back is arguing at one of them.
She offers Elsie the half of her slate she has not used; the axe is Margery.
The Copper Hounds dropped Tamsin this morning, over the shield-bearer's arm.
Elsie's hand goes flat on Tamsin's wrist; Tamsin goes still, and her ears are red.
Elsie asks whether the arm is mending; Tamsin stares, and says probably.
A small woman in brass goggles, Ottilie Brandt called Tilly, comes out talking fast.
Thrown out of the Alchemists' College, she answers what she brews with three warnings.
Tilly goes red to the ears when Elsie smiles, and drops her chalk twice.
Tamsin's guild notice: six lanterns for the apothecary, moonbells at the Glasswood.
Elsie says the three could take it; Tamsin asks if she has been in a dungeon.
Elsie chalks three names on the last slate; Tilly writes hers under, then Tamsin.
Tilly asks her class; Elsie says Enthraller and does not look away.
Tamsin says, so you can make me do anything; Elsie says that is not how hers works.
Tilly asks about bonds; Cora watches the wrist, the chalk, the red ears, and writes nothing.
The lamplighters' boats move along the canal, and the lanterns come on one by one.
Elsie thinks the three of them are going to be friends, and is glad enough to hum.
Cora opens the black ledger, writes nothing, and puts it back under her coat.
Asked what she will write, Cora says she has not decided.
Elsie says she will try to give her something good to write.
